slides.summary: Retired teacher Jim Crouch has grown and given away 10,000 oak seedlings across Southern California, opening a sixth nursery to help replant fire-scarred Altadena.

slides.summary: Ahmed and Rifat Ali's home, condemned after they lost £72,000 to an unsafe extension, was rebuilt by more than 150 tradespeople and volunteers on BBC's DIY SOS, with cameras, visual fire and doorbell alerts and color changing lights built in for their deaf family.
slides.headline: Home rebuilt for deaf family on BBC DIY SOS

slides.summary: Stanford scientists reversed cartilage loss and blocked arthritis in mice by inhibiting a single aging-related protein, and human knee cartilage samples began growing new tissue in response.
slides.headline: Stanford scientists reverse cartilage loss in mice
slides.proves: Human cartilage taken during knee replacement surgery responded to the same treatment by producing new, functional cartilage.

picture.query: Stanford scientists reversed cartilage loss and blocked arthritis

slides.summary: All 32 patients in the NEOPRISM-CRC trial stayed free of bowel cancer recurrence for 33 months after a nine week course of pembrolizumab before surgery, far beating the 25% relapse rate expected with standard chemotherapy.
slides.headline: Pembrolizumab keeps bowel cancer in remission for 33 months
slides.proves: Blood tests tracking tumor DNA could let doctors identify which patients can safely skip extra chemotherapy after surgery.

slides.summary: Ukraine has expanded free hot school lunches to every grade 1 to 11 student, now feeding roughly 3 million children daily, with kitchens in frontline Sumy region cooking through air raid sirens and blackouts.
slides.headline: Ukraine expands free hot lunches to 3 million students
slides.proves: A diesel generator at Romny School No. 7 shows how a single kitchen can keep cooking through Russian strikes on the power grid.
